audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Darius/Darius/Skill/Darius/Skill/Darius/Darius. The published Darius-side audit sets this matchup as Darius through Levels 4-5 and Maokai from Level 6 on, and the page's own whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] describe exactly that swing while the chart still gave Darius first item and two items.
audit.why: The mirror is already on disk; any disagreement I leave here gets overwritten by mirror-fix.js, and until then the page tells a 52.4% Maokai he loses the stages his own text says he wins.
audit.corrected: Rows 2,4,5,6 flipped in both layers so the chart reads Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai; ratings adjusted from Maokai's side; whys[2] rewritten so the Level 3 row and its reason agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is the page's focus ability and never carried a cooldown.
audit.why: It is 26s at rank 1 — by far the longest timer in the lane and his only engage. That single number is the whole trading plan, and it drops to 16s by rank 5.
audit.corrected: tldr, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and mid now state 26s and key the commit to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance's untargetable flight was never stated, and the anti-heal advice sat after the chip rather than before it.
audit.why: A Noxian Guillotine cast into the dash finds no target. And Sap Magic's cooldown shortens each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by one, so Darius's own poke charges the heal — Grievous Wounds has to be bought before the grind, not after.
audit.corrected: report[5].t states the untargetable dash; breakdown.cooldowns adds it; mid moves Grievous Wounds ahead of the grind; late states the Sap Magic acceleration.

edits.before: Survive his early — W-peel his pull, sustain up. Maokai wins the Apprehend cooldown windows.
edits.after: Survive his early — W-peel his pull, sustain up. Maokai wins the 26s after Apprehend.

edits.before: His all-in start. W-peel after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 26s at rank 1 — a whiffed Apprehend is your whole trading window.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — His all-in start. W-peel after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1, the longest timer in the lane and his only engage — a whiffed pull is a free wave for you. - Noxian Guillotine: 120s, but it refreshes on a kill. - Twisted Advance: 14s and untargetable in flight.

edits.before: Track Darius's Apprehend (Pull): His all-in start. W-peel after it. When it is down — W-Q + R him.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight — a Guillotine cast into the dash finds nothing.

edits.before: Once you complete W (Twisted Advance) into Q with Sap Magic healing, you finally have a trade that answers his step-up — it's a genuine coinflip on who lands first.
edits.after: W (Twisted Advance) into Q with Sap Magic finally answers his step-up, but Decimate's blade edge and stacked bleed still take the extended trade at 3.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip decided by who lands their setup first — if he E-pulls you onto a wave with his Q up, his bleed still out-damages you, but if you W-root him as he steps to last-hit, your Q knockback plus Sap Magic heal grinds the trade your way. Bait his E: when it's on cooldown he can't initiate the all-in, so that's your window to W in. At 6 your R (Nature's Grasp) doesn't burst him, but the long-range root lets you lock the all-in down or set up your jungler — you stop fleeing his melee threat and start playing the lane even.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are decided by who lands their setup first — if he Apprehends you onto a wave with Decimate up his bleed still out-damages you, but if you W-root him as he steps to last-hit, your Q knockback plus Sap Magic heal grinds the trade your way. Bait the pull: 26s at rank 1, and without it he cannot start the all-in, so that gap is your window to W in. At 6 Nature's Grasp doesn't burst him, but the long-range root locks his all-in down — and buy Grievous Wounds before you try to grind him, not after.

edits.before: This is where the 52.4% comes from — once your first tank item and stacked resistances come online, his Hemorrhage bleed and R execute stop punching through, and Sap Magic heals back what his Q chips. You'll never out-burst Darius in a raw melee all-in, but you don't need to: you root him with W, peel with Q, and your R turns every skirmish into a 5v5 your team wins on CC. Don't ego the straight 1v1 when he has 5 bleed stacks up — make him fight you in the brambles, not the open lane.
edits.after: This is where the 52.4% comes from — once your first tank item and stacked resistances land, Hemorrhage and the execute stop punching through, and Sap Magic heals back what Decimate chips; every spell he lands on you shortens that heal's cooldown. You'll never out-burst Darius in a raw melee all-in, but you don't need to: root with W, peel with Q, and your R turns each skirmish into a 5v5 your team wins on CC. Don't ego the 1v1 at five bleed stacks — make him fight you in the brambles.
